lessons.title: Server Execution via Node.js Runtime
lessons.description: Run JavaScript outside the browser using Node.js — build servers, APIs and command-line tools.

sections.heading: What is Node.js?
paragraphs: Node.js is a JavaScript runtime built on V8 that runs outside the browser. It gives you access to the file system, network, operating system and more — everything you need to build server-side applications.
list: Runs JavaScript outside the browser using the V8 engine
Provides APIs for file I/O, networking, processes and more
Uses an event loop for non-blocking I/O (same concept as the browser)
npm gives access to over 1 million packages

codeExamples.heading: Your first Node.js script
explanation: require() imports built-in modules (no installation needed).
fs.readFile reads files asynchronously with a callback.
__dirname gives you the current script's directory.

practice.task: Create a Node.js script that reads a JSON file and logs its contents to the console.

keyTakeaways: Node.js runs JavaScript outside the browser using the V8 engine.
It provides built-in modules for file I/O, networking and system operations.
npm gives access to a massive ecosystem of packages.
Node.js uses the same event loop concept as the browser.
lessons.challenge: Build a command-line tool that reads a CSV file and outputs the total number of rows.

lessons.title: Node Core Modules: fs/promises, path, http
lessons.description: Master the essential built-in modules: file system, path manipulation and HTTP server creation.

sections.heading: Core modules
list: http — create HTTP servers and make requests

codeExamples.heading: HTTP server with built-in modules
explanation: http.createServer creates a basic HTTP server.
The callback receives every request with req and res objects.
fs/promises reads files asynchronously with async/await.

practice.task: Create a Node.js HTTP server that serves different responses for /, /about, and /api/time routes.
hints: /api/time should return the current time as JSON.

keyTakeaways: fs/promises provides async file operations with modern async/await.
path handles cross-platform file paths safely.
http.createServer builds basic HTTP servers without frameworks.
Always set Content-Type headers and handle 404 errors.
lessons.challenge: Build a static file server using only Node.js built-in modules (no Express).

lessons.title: Building REST APIs using Express / Fastify
lessons.description: Express is the most popular Node.js framework for building REST APIs — clean routing, middleware and more.

sections.heading: Express basics
list: express.json() — middleware to parse JSON request bodies

codeExamples.heading: Express REST API
explanation: express.json() middleware parses JSON request bodies.
Route parameters like :id are available via req.params.
res.json() sends a JSON response with proper headers.
res.status() sets the HTTP status code.

practice.task: Build a complete REST API for a todo list with GET, POST, PUT and DELETE endpoints using Express.

keyTakeaways: Express simplifies HTTP server creation with clean routing syntax.
Middleware adds functionality like JSON parsing, logging and authentication.
Route parameters capture dynamic URL segments.
Always return proper HTTP status codes and Content-Type headers.
lessons.challenge: Build a REST API for a blog with posts, comments and users — including validation and error handling.
